title: Seven-Word Subcore Exclusions and a Six-Hole Plateau in the Ternary Covering Problem K_3(7,3)
description: Technical report, software, and reproducible finite computations for scoped structural exclusions in the unresolved ternary covering-code problem K_3(7,3). For each of eight seven-word subcores obtained by deleting one word from an explicit eight-word core, every set of at most four added centers leaves at least six radius-3 holes, and equality is attained. Consequently, no size-at-most-11 covering code contains any of these subcores or an isometric copy. Independent Rust and C++20 implementations verify the four deletion-orbit representatives by exact pair reduction, building 9,500,440 pair entries and querying 347,365 eligible first pairs. The release also classifies the exact three-center completions of the eight-word core, an exact six-hole replacement plateau, and a diameter-at-most-4 lower bound of 17. The global interval 11 <= K_3(7,3) <= 12 remains unchanged.
